name: Ladybug
intro: A ladybug is a small, round beetle. Many ladybugs are red with black spots.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A ladybug is a small, round beetle.
Many ladybugs are red or orange with black spots.
Some ladybugs have stripes or no spots at all.
It has six short legs.
Hard wing covers keep its thin flying wings safe.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Ladybugs live in many parts of the world.
They live in gardens, fields, and forests.
In winter, many ladybugs rest together in big groups.
They hide under logs, under rocks, or in houses.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Most ladybugs eat tiny bugs called aphids.
Aphids eat plants.
One ladybug can eat lots of aphids in one day.
Ladybugs help gardeners keep plants healthy.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A mother ladybug lays tiny eggs under a leaf.
She lays them near aphids.
A larva hatches out in a few days.
The larva is long and spiky, not round.
It becomes a pupa, then a grown-up ladybug.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Bright colors tell birds that ladybugs taste bad.
A scared ladybug may play dead.
Four ladybugs once rode on a space shuttle.
Ladybugs are the state insect of five states.
Many people think ladybugs bring good luck.

vocab.meaning: An insect with hard covers over its wings.
A tiny bug that eats plants.
A baby insect that does not look like its parents yet.
The resting stage when a young insect changes into a grown-up.
